title: Elektro at the World's Fair
summary: A voice-command demonstration robot showed the public a mechanical imitation of human actions, using relays and prerecorded speech.

title: Konrad Zuse finishes the Z3 Computer
summary: Zuse completed a relay-based programmable computer, bringing automated binary arithmetic to engineering calculations.

title: Public unveiling of ENIAC
summary: The public unveiling of ENIAC demonstrated the potential of electronic computing for large calculation workloads.

title: Manchester Mark I Williams-Kilburn tube
summary: Williams and Kilburn developed electronic memory using a cathode-ray tube, helping make stored-program computing practical.

title: Cybernetics
summary: Wiener connected feedback, communication and control in a framework that influenced automation and artificial intelligence research.

title: The Mathematical Theory of Communication
summary: Shannon formalized information and communication limits, providing foundational tools for digital communication systems.

title: First Computer Program to Run on a Computer
summary: The Manchester Baby ran a stored program, demonstrating that instructions could reside in electronic memory alongside data.

title: First Univac 1 delivered to US Census Bureau
summary: UNIVAC reached the US Census Bureau, illustrating the transition from experimental computation to institutional data processing.

title: J. Lyons & Company introduce LEO-1
summary: LEO applied electronic computing to business scheduling, connecting digital calculations to everyday operations.

title: Grace Hopper completes A-0
summary: Hopper developed A-0, an early step toward translating higher-level instructions into computer operations.

title: Grimsdale and Webb build early transistorized computer
summary: A prototype transistorized computer demonstrated an alternative to vacuum-tube computing hardware.

title: Whirlwind core memory
summary: MIT installed magnetic core memory in Whirlwind, advancing reliable electronic data storage.

title: IBM 650 magnetic drum calculator introduced
summary: IBM introduced a widely adopted drum-memory computer that helped institutions and universities use electronic data processing.

title: RAMAC
summary: RAMAC introduced commercial magnetic disk storage, making data directly accessible rather than requiring sequential retrieval.

title: FORTRAN
summary: FORTRAN made scientific programming more accessible by translating symbolic statements into efficient machine instructions.

title: First computer scanned image on SEAC
summary: A SEAC team digitized an image, opening a path toward computer-based image processing.

title: LISP
summary: LISP represented programs and data as lists, providing a language suited to symbolic artificial intelligence research.

title: SAGE system goes online
summary: SAGE connected computing with radar and operational coordination, showing the possibilities and demands of large real-time systems.

title: Compatible Time-Sharing System (CTSS) is Demonstrated
summary: CTSS demonstrated interactive shared computer use, allowing users to work through terminals instead of only batch jobs.

title: UNIMATE
summary: UNIMATE brought programmable industrial robotics into factory work, changing the relationship between machinery and production labour.

title: Spacewar! debuts
summary: Spacewar! demonstrated interactive computer entertainment and real-time graphics on a research computer.

title: ASCII
summary: ASCII standardized character encoding, easing exchange of text between different computing systems.

title: Ivan Sutherland publishes Sketchpad
summary: Sketchpad demonstrated interactive graphical design, influencing computer-aided design and human-computer interaction.

title: IBM announces System/360
summary: System/360 offered a compatible computer family, allowing institutions to expand computing while retaining software investments.

title: Thomas Kurtz and John Kemeny create BASIC
summary: BASIC was developed to broaden access to programming, particularly in education.

title: DENDRAL artificial intelligence program
summary: DENDRAL explored knowledge-based problem solving in chemistry, demonstrating a specialized approach to artificial intelligence.

title: The Mother of All Demos
summary: Engelbart demonstrated interactive tools including the mouse and collaborative document work, illustrating computing as human augmentation.

title: Hooking up – networks come online
summary: Early packet networks connected computers, laying groundwork for shared digital infrastructure.

title: Kenneth Thompson and Dennis Ritchie develop UNIX
summary: Thompson and Ritchie began UNIX, a system whose design influenced decades of software and operating-system development.

title: Intel introduces the first microprocessor
summary: Intel introduced a microprocessor, concentrating processing functions on a chip and expanding opportunities for embedded computation.

title: Networked Email as an Early “Killer App”
summary: Network email provided a practical communication use for connected computers.

title: C programming language is released
summary: C provided a systems programming language that would become central to operating systems and software infrastructure.

title: Linking the Office: Ethernet and Local Networks
summary: Ethernet research connected computers locally, helping move offices toward shared network resources.

title: MITS Altair 8800 kit appears in Popular Electronics
summary: The Altair kit made microcomputer experimentation available to a growing community of enthusiasts.

title: Steve Wozniak completes the Apple-1
summary: The Apple-1 connected microcomputer design with a nascent personal-computing market.

title: Apple II introduced
summary: The Apple II helped bring computing into homes, schools and small businesses.

title: Visicalc is developed
summary: VisiCalc demonstrated personal-computer spreadsheet work, making digital tools useful for business planning.

title: IBM introduces its Personal Computer (PC)
summary: IBM introduced its personal computer, contributing to a broad ecosystem of compatible hardware and software.

title: Richard Stallman develops GNU
summary: The GNU project sought a freely usable operating-system environment, influencing collaborative software development.

title: Apple Computer launches the Macintosh
summary: The Macintosh brought a graphical interface and mouse interaction to a wider personal-computing audience.

title: The "WorldWideWeb" is born
summary: Berners-Lee developed the WorldWideWeb browser and server, joining hypertext documents with network access.

title: Linus Torvalds releases the Linux kernel
summary: Torvalds released the Linux kernel, enabling an expanding ecosystem of openly developed computing infrastructure.

title: Mosaic popularizes the Web
summary: Mosaic helped make the Web easier to navigate through a graphical browser.

title: JavaScript is developed
summary: JavaScript added programmable behaviour to browser pages, changing the Web from documents toward interactive applications.

title: Deep Blue defeats Garry Kasparov
summary: Deep Blue defeated Kasparov in a chess match, demonstrating specialized search and evaluation rather than general human-level intelligence.

title: Opportunity and Spirit Mars Rovers land on Mars
summary: The Spirit and Opportunity rovers extended robotic exploration of Mars through remotely coordinated operations.

title: Stanford's autonomous vehicle wins 2005 DARPA “Grand Challenge”
summary: A Stanford autonomous vehicle won the DARPA Grand Challenge, demonstrating progress in robotic navigation in a bounded competition.

title: The Apple iPhone is released
summary: The iPhone joined mobile communication, touch interaction and Internet access in a consumer handheld device.

title: Nvidia releases Cuda GPU
summary: CUDA made graphics processors available for general-purpose parallel computing, later supporting machine-learning workloads.

title: Raspberry Pi, a credit-card-size single board computer, is released as a tool to promote science education
summary: Raspberry Pi made low-cost programmable computing hardware accessible for education and experimentation.

title: First transatlantic wireless signals
summary: Marconi transmitted wireless signals across the Atlantic in December 1901, demonstrating long-distance radio communication.

title: Wright Flyer demonstrates powered flight
publisher: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
summary: The Wright brothers demonstrated powered flight in 1903, opening a new relationship between transport and engineering.

title: Ford introduces moving assembly line
summary: The moving assembly line brought work to workers, changing manufacturing organization and production speed.

title: Fleming discovers penicillin
summary: Fleming observed an antibacterial mould in 1928; subsequent development would transform infection treatment.

title: AlexNet demonstrates deep image classification
summary: The published convolutional-network research advanced large-scale image classification.

title: Attention Is All You Need submitted
summary: The Transformer architecture introduced attention-based sequence modelling without recurrence.

title: GPT-3 research paper submitted
summary: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners described large-scale language modelling and few-shot task adaptation.

title: Point-contact transistor demonstrated
summary: Bardeen and Brattain achieved semiconductor amplification, a foundation for compact electronic devices.

title: Dartmouth artificial intelligence research workshop
summary: A summer research project helped establish artificial intelligence as a named field of inquiry.

title: Apollo 11 lunar landing
summary: Apollo 11 brought humans to the lunar surface through a combination of engineering, computation and human operations.

title: World Wide Web proposal circulated
summary: Berners-Lee proposed a linked information system at CERN, laying groundwork for a global hypertext network.

title: Web announced on alt.hypertext
summary: The Web project was shared through an Internet discussion group, inviting wider participation beyond CERN.

title: AlphaGo defeats Lee Sedol
summary: AlphaGo won a Go match against Lee Sedol. This demonstrated specialized learning and search, not universal autonomy.

title: GPT-4 technical report submitted
summary: The technical report documented a large multimodal model and its capabilities and limitations. This is the report submission date, not the product launch date.

title: GPT-4o system card submitted to arXiv
summary: The system card documented multimodal capabilities and safety evaluations. This is the arXiv submission date, not the model launch date.

title: DeepSeek-R1 research submitted
summary: Researchers reported reinforcement-learning methods for reasoning tasks. Reported results concern evaluated tasks, not a guarantee of general reliability.

title: π0.5 robot generalization research submitted
summary: Researchers described a vision-language-action model and experiments with household manipulation in new homes. Research demonstrations do not establish broad unsupervised deployment.
